answers.question: I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?
answers.answer:
No, not at this level next week. Feeling fine during a run does not show the load is absorbed, and a jump of about 40 percent in weekly miles needs a step back before more volume.

Next week runs about 39 miles, with three threshold reps and a 14-mile long run. From the week of Sep 21 the volume builds again gradually, with marathon-pace work in some long runs once the calves feel settled.

new.analysis:
## Why the week ran over
The plan asked for about 38 miles, and the week came in at 53, about 40 percent more than the 37 miles of the week before. Most of the extra came from running longer than planned on several days and from the 20-mile long run, not from the one quality session.

| Measure | Plan | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Distance | 38 mi | 53 mi |
| Long run | 15 mi | 20 mi |
| Threshold reps | 3 | 4 |
| Easy share of time | 80 percent or more | 54 percent |

The long run was the hardest effort of the week, not an easy one. An average heart rate of 149 and effort 7/10 over 20 miles, with the heart rate climbing 7 beats, show the body was working hard in the second half. Running with two club members and carrying on past the planned 15 miles added time at an effort the plan did not call for.

The easy share fell well below the 80 percent target because the long run and the threshold session added time in higher zones. The easy runs themselves held steady at about 139 beats and 9:50 per mile, so the aerobic base is responding well.

Feeling fine during the runs does not show the load is absorbed. The calves were tight Sunday night, and tightness after a jump this size is worth taking seriously before adding more volume. That is why next week steps back rather than holds.

The threshold session should have stopped at three reps. The fourth rep was added because it felt strong, but the reps at 8:00 per mile already run faster than marathon pace, about 8:35 per mile for a 3:45 finish. Extra reps add stress faster than they add benefit.

Next week keeps the same structure and trims the miles to about 39, a short step back from the 53 run and just above the original 38. The 14-mile long run keeps the weekly long-run habit while giving the legs room to settle. Marathon-pace segments wait until the long run feels settled, likely in the week of Sep 21.
